clue.text: Joke book?

definitions.meaning: to joke is to tease or kid playfully
the Old Testament book of Joshua is abbreviated this way

explanation.definitionFit: Teasing banter is a gentle jest, and the Bible's book of Joshua is shortened to these four letters.

clue.text: Copperfield begging

parts.note: the Dickens name splits as copper, a penny (abbreviated P), and field, a lea or meadow, and that run joined means an appeal, as begging does

explanation.surface: The Dickens hero David Copperfield, reduced to begging.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word Copperfield must be split into copper (P, a penny) and field (LEA); begging is the definition, a type of split the grammar can only file as a whole-clue reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An urgent request or appeal is the noun sense of begging.

clue.text: Duke, say, holding western dollars

parts.note: dukes is slang for clenched hands, and one clutching money recalls the Clint Eastwood western titled for a handful of dollars

explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up your dukes' means raise your hands to fight; the western is A ___ful of Dollars.
explanation.definitionFit: A clenched hand is called a duke in boxing slang, and the film title pictures it full of cash.

clue.text: Clearness of water run in LA, city of variety

indicators.note: run is placed inside the jumbled letters of the place name
a variety of arrangements suggests the letters of LA and city are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A remark on how clean the water is in Los Angeles, a varied city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearness of water' is the definition, and 'of variety' is the anagram signal, not part of the city description.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparency in a liquid is what makes it look clear.

clue.text: Chemist once knotted a yacht-rope

indicators.note: a knotted rope is twisted up, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An old pharmacist has tied knots in a yachting rope.
explanation.walkthrough: An apothecary was the old name for a pharmacist; 'once' marks the term as dated.
explanation.definitionFit: Before modern pharmacy, a druggist who made and sold medicines went by this old title.

clue.text: Sliced loaf ordered for mining areas

indicators.note: put into order, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sliced loaf ordered for miners' districts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges SLICED LOAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions where coal is dug from the ground are its producing districts.

clue.text: But don't expect it to have a cube root!

definitions.text: But don't expect it to have a cube root!

parts.words: But don't expect it to have a cube root!
parts.note: a play on cube root in mathematics: this root crop yields what is pressed into cubes, yet it does not grow as cubes itself

explanation.walkthrough: A cube root sounds mathematical, but here 'root' is a vegetable whose product is sold as lumps for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: This root vegetable is processed into the sweetener sold as cubes, though the root itself is not cube-shaped.

clue.text: News of an anaesthetic

definitions.meaning: inside information or the latest gen
slang for a drug, especially one that dulls the senses

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang both for inside information and for a drug that dulls the senses.

clue.text: CID dreads being turned out and dumped

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are tipped out and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Fearful detectives are being turned out of their jobs and dumped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being turned out' rearranges CID and DREADS; CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing something away as unwanted is getting rid of it.

clue.text: Matting wicket for cricket at home?

definitions.text: Matting wicket for cricket at home?

parts.words: Matting wicket for cricket at home?
parts.note: a matting wicket is a mat cricket is played on; Dickens wrote of The Cricket on the Hearth, so the insect's pitch is a rug by the fireplace

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket here is the insect from Dickens's The Cricket on the Hearth, not the sport; its 'matting wicket' is a mat laid before the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat laid before a fireplace is where a domestic cricket might chirp.

clue.text: Fabulous creature taking up the French horn

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: cor is the French word for a horn

explanation.surface: A mythical beast is learning the French horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking up' reverses COR, French for horn, in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant bird of Arabian legend, as in Sinbad's voyages, is a creature of fable.

clue.text: Place is a mess, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word for a mess is taken by its sound

parts.note: a sight is something that looks a mess, as in 'you look a sight'

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a location is untidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You look a sight' means you look a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or spot where something stands is its plot or position.

clue.text: A church seen on short section of Circle Line

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic, a church

explanation.surface: A church is visible beside part of London's Underground Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here it is just the curved line of a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry, part of a circle's circumference is a curved segment.

clue.text: Breed of sheep from Dudley

definitions.meaning: a long-wool English sheep named after a Midlands county
Robert Dudley was Elizabeth I's favourite, created Earl of this title

explanation.definitionFit: A long-woolled English sheep shares its name with the earldom given to Robert Dudley, Elizabeth I's favourite.

clue.text: Aid to angler, winning with clear profit

parts.note: landing a contract or prize is winning it
net profit is what remains after costs

explanation.surface: A fisherman's gadget brings success and a clear profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman uses a mesh bag on a pole to lift a hooked catch from the water.

clue.text: Club functions in casting premises?

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
works means functions or operates

explanation.surface: A golf club operates inside a film casting studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casting' suggests choosing actors, but it is pouring metal into moulds.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundry, where metal is smelted and cast, is a factory of this kind.

clue.text: Throw flowers around a river in this blessed plot?

indicators.note: the article and river go inside the name of the country

parts.note: Shakespeare's Richard II calls the country 'this blessed plot, this earth, this realm'

explanation.surface: Someone scatters blossoms around a river in a sacred piece of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This blessed plot' is John of Gaunt's speech in Shakespeare's Richard II about his country.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreathe or encircle someone with garlands is to put flowers around them.

clue.text: A place of retreat in port

parts.note: a den is a private room or lair to withdraw to

explanation.surface: A secluded refuge somewhere in a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yemeni city on the Gulf of its name is a major harbour.

clue.text: Stuff with pieces of chicken — gorgeous!

indicators.note: only parts of these words are taken, the run of letters lying across them

explanation.surface: Someone gorging on chicken pieces declares them gorgeous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces of' takes the run chickEN GORGEous.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge or fill to excess is to cram full.

clue.text: Progress in main road

parts.note: head as an adjective means chief or main
way is a road or path

explanation.surface: Moving forward on the main road.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward movement toward a goal is advancement.

clue.text: Harry has little work on the papers

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work of music
the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: A man named Harry writes a short piece for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a man's name but is the verb meaning to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass or persecute persistently, to bear down on cruelly.

clue.text: Outlook of woman after life in France?

indicators.note: the letter for woman follows the French word

parts.note: vie is the French word for life

explanation.surface: A woman's perspective on living in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A perspective or prospect is a way of seeing things.

clue.text: Type ruled out, seemingly

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their original order

explanation.surface: A printing typeface is excluded, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TYPE RULED.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently, according to what people say or believe, is the sense.

clue.text: Therefore, run away with self-confidence

indicators.note: away tells us the letter for run goes from the Latin word

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: So someone runs off with their self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R (run) from ERGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-esteem or one's sense of personal worth is what this word names.

clue.text: One swoops low, nose to tail

indicators.note: the front letter of the word is moved to the back, as nose moves to tail

explanation.surface: A creature swoops down low, nose to tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nose to tail' moves the L of LOW to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This nocturnal bird of prey dives down on its prey.

clue.text: Gummy agent backing Indian music

indicators.note: backing means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a raga is a melodic pattern in Indian classical music

explanation.surface: A sticky representative is supporting Indian music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agent' suggests a person, but it is a substance; 'backing' suggests support.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly from seaweed is used as a thickening or setting substance.

clue.text: Tourists in Greece see this-a harvest, silo-treated

parts.note: a crop is a harvest

indicators.note: treated means processed, so the letters of silo are rearranged

explanation.surface: Visitors in Greece view a farm harvest being handled in a silo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges SILO into OLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient citadel above Athens is the most visited sight in the country.

clue.text: Ghosts, for instance, in the theatre?

definitions.text: Ghosts, for instance, in the theatre?

parts.words: Ghosts, for instance, in the theatre?
parts.note: Ghosts is a drama by Ibsen, though spectres in a theatre sound like hauntings

explanation.walkthrough: Ghosts is the title of Henrik Ibsen's drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's Ghosts is a stage drama, an example of a work performed in a theatre.

clue.text: Garlands of Hawaiian exotic isle

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters of isle are rearranged

explanation.surface: Flower garlands from a Hawaiian island far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges ISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaiian flower necklaces are given to visitors as welcome wreaths.

clue.text: Single walking-on part

definitions.meaning: the underside of the foot, what one walks on

explanation.definitionFit: The word means only or lone, and also the underside of the foot that we tread on.

clue.text: Place in which to eat hash

definitions.meaning: making a hash of something is a muddle

explanation.definitionFit: A military dining hall, and also a muddle or botch.

clue.text: Attractive girl liable to change into something more comfortable

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: to change means the letters of liable are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A pretty girl is likely to slip into something more comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges LIABLE into ABILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of being partly or casually dressed is loose informal attire.
